main.description: Declaration record for an academic profile. Fixed rkey 'self' -- per the atproto Lexicon style guide, a single-instance declaration record marks an account as participating in this app modality, and deleting it signals departure. Holds only identity and cross-registry identifiers; every substantive CV section is its own record type.

displayName.description: Name as it should appear on a CV, in the profile's primary locale.

nativeName.description: Name in the native script, e.g. '山田 太郎', when displayName is romanised. Both are needed: publications appear under both forms.

namePreferredCitation.description: How the person prefers to be cited, e.g. 'T. Yamada'. Disambiguation matters more here than aesthetics.

headline.description: One line, e.g. 'Assistant Professor of Computational Biology'.

orcid.description: Bare ORCID iD. The single most useful field here: it is the bridge to every existing scholarly registry.

researchmapId.description: researchmap permalink ID. Effectively mandatory in Japan.

kakenId.description: JSPS 研究者番号 (8 digits). Required on every Japanese grant application.

acceptingStudents.description: Whether the person is currently taking on graduate students. Cheap to store, genuinely useful to prospective students, and absent from every existing registry.

jglobalId.description: J-GLOBAL ID, e.g. '201701013771755270'. Assigned by JST and cross-referenced by most Japanese research administration systems.

researchmapMemberId.description: researchmap 会員ID, e.g. 'B000285141'. Distinct from researchmapId, which is the URL permalink.

degrees.description: Degrees held, as printed in the 学位 field of a Japanese profile ('工学博士(名古屋大学)'). Duplicates information in id.career.education on purpose: the education record describes a period of study, this is the standing credential, and Japanese application forms ask for the latter without the former.

educationRef.description: StrongRef to the id.career.education record this credential came from, when one exists.
